title: Student identity is directly disclosed with the submission
description: The student sends a student identifier together with the assignment file, course, and submission timestamp. This directly reveals the submitter's identity to the receiving system as part of the flow.
assumptions: The student identifier is unique or reasonably attributable to a specific student.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context did not include detailed threat-tree nodes.

title: Submission metadata can link multiple submissions to the same student
description: Data in transit includes student id, course, and submission timestamp. Together these attributes can be used to correlate multiple submissions and activities of the same student across time and courses.
assumptions: The flow metadata or payload is observable by an intermediary or logged along the transmission path.
uncertainty_note: Applicable as a data-in-transit/linkability concern if transport-path observers, intermediaries, or network/application logs can access payload or metadata.

title: Submission timing and course context expose student activity patterns in transit
description: Even aside from the file contents, the combination of submission timestamp, course, and sender/recipient context can reveal that a particular student is active in a specific course at a specific time.
assumptions: An observer of the flow can access payload fields or sufficiently rich communication metadata.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is approximate; disclosure here is grounded in exposure of personal activity metadata on the flow.

title: Received assignment contents may disclose additional personal information
description: On receipt, the portal processes and stores the uploaded work file, which may contain personal data beyond what is necessary for submission, such as the student's name in the document body, document metadata, comments, or embedded identifiers.
assumptions: The portal stores or makes available the full uploaded file and its metadata.
uncertainty_note: Threat is at the destination because the receiving process handles and potentially persists the full file and metadata.

title: Student may be unaware of secondary use or retention of submission data
description: The portal receives the assignment file, student id, course, and timestamp, but the student may not understand how long these data are retained, who can access them, or whether they are reused for plagiarism detection, analytics, or auditing.
assumptions: The portal's privacy notice or submission interface does not fully explain retention, access, and downstream uses.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible unawareness threat at the destination, but it depends on the actual transparency provided by the portal.

title: Submission may be processed beyond the student's consent or expected purpose
description: After receiving the submission, the portal could process or share the assignment and associated identifiers for purposes beyond assignment handling, such as analytics, model training, or extended retention, without a consent basis or another appropriate legal basis aligned with the student's expectations.
assumptions: There is no clearly established lawful basis, or processing extends beyond what was communicated and justified.
uncertainty_note: Framed as non-compliance risk at the destination; actual applicability depends on the system's governance, notices, contracts, and legal basis.

title: Portal shares identified student data with grading service
description: The portal forwards student id together with course, file reference, and requesting role to the assignment & grading service. Because the source process discloses identified data to another process, the act of sharing creates an identifying threat.
assumptions: Student id is unique within the institution and directly or indirectly identifies the student.

title: Identifiers are present on the flow in transit
description: The data flow carries a student id, which is a unique reference to the data subject. Anyone able to observe the flow or its contents can identify the student from the transmitted identifier.
assumptions: The student id is exposed on the flow payload or otherwise available to parties observing the transmission.

title: Submission and grading requests can link student activity across contexts
description: Combining student id with course, file reference, and requesting role on this flow enables correlation of multiple requests to the same student across assignments or courses, supporting linkage of actions and records.
assumptions: The same student id is reused across requests and can be correlated over time.
uncertainty_note: Threat-tree node cited at a higher-level linkage node because the exact subnode was not provided in retrieved context.

title: Received submission/grading requests may become evidence attributable to a student
description: Once the assignment & grading service receives identified submission or grading requests, it may retain records showing that a particular student submitted work or was subject to grading actions. Such records can reduce the student's ability to deny involvement in those actions.
assumptions: P2 logs or stores request details with sufficient integrity and attribution to be used as evidence.
uncertainty_note: Exact Nr subnode is approximate because the retrieved context only described the threat type, not the detailed tree.

title: Grading service can infer student academic activity from received request data
description: From student id, course, file reference, and requesting role, the destination can infer that a specific student is enrolled in a course, is submitting coursework, and is participating in grading-related processes. This reveals personal aspects of academic behavior beyond the immediate routing purpose.
assumptions: P2 can inspect and retain the semantic meaning of course and file-reference data.
uncertainty_note: Exact detectability/disclosure subnode is approximate because no detailed D-tree node was retrieved.

title: Excessive disclosure when storing assignment submission metadata
description: The grading service stores the submitted assignment together with student id, course, and submission time. If all of these attributes are not strictly necessary for grading or later academic administration, the act of sending them to persistent storage constitutes avoidable disclosure of personal data beyond the minimum necessary.
assumptions: Assumes at least some stored attributes or their granularity may exceed what is strictly required for the stated purpose.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-judgement based on LINDDUN Pro data-disclosure/minimality concepts; exact subnode may differ in the canonical tree.

title: Stored submission records enable linking across assignments or courses
description: By receiving and storing student id together with course and submission time, the assignment store can enable correlation of multiple submissions belonging to the same student across assignments, courses, or time periods. This creates a linkability risk if records are retained or queried in a way that allows building longitudinal profiles.
assumptions: Assumes the datastore preserves identifiers and metadata in a form that supports cross-record correlation.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; the applicability of linkability is strong, but the precise subnode may vary by tree version.

title: Student identity can be inferred directly from stored submission data
description: Because the stored record includes a student id, the destination datastore holds directly identifying information tied to a specific assignment submission. Anyone with access to the store, or any downstream process using it, can identify the submitting student from the stored data.
assumptions: Assumes student id is directly identifying within the system context or can readily be resolved to a person.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node id is approximate; identification clearly applies, but the canonical subnode label may differ.

title: Stored submission metadata reveals student behavior and activity patterns
description: Submission time, course association, and repeated stored submissions can reveal personal aspects of a student's behavior, such as working patterns, lateness, participation level, or course load. The datastore's receipt and retention of these attributes therefore creates a detectability risk regarding the student's activities.
assumptions: Assumes authorized or unauthorized observers can inspect records or metadata in the store.
uncertainty_note: Detectability is plausible here through stored metadata, but whether LINDDUN would prioritize D over other categories for this flow is somewhat context-dependent.

title: Persistent storage may exceed the consented or expected purpose
description: If students were not clearly informed that their assignment file, student id, course, and precise submission time would be stored in this datastore, or if storage/retention goes beyond the original educational purpose, the destination processing may violate consent and transparency expectations.
assumptions: Assumes consent, notice, or purpose limitation for this storage is incomplete, ambiguous, or broader than necessary.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends heavily on organizational notice, legal basis, and retention policy, which are not provided.

title: Teacher submits identified login/request data
description: The teacher initiates the interaction by sending identified account or session-related data to request the review queue. If the request uses directly identifying attributes such as username, email address, employee ID, or a stable account identifier, the teacher is identifiable from this flow.
assumptions: Assumes the login/request contains direct identifiers or stable account identifiers rather than fully anonymous credentials.

title: Request metadata can link teacher activity across sessions
description: Metadata on the flow, such as source IP address, device/browser fingerprint, course-selection patterns, timestamps, and repeated account/session identifiers, can allow linking multiple requests to the same teacher over time, revealing patterns of grading activity.
assumptions: Assumes network/application metadata or stable identifiers are observable in transit or by intermediaries.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; retrieved context did not include the specific linkability subtree.

title: Data in transit identifies the teacher
description: The login/request flow may contain direct identifiers or stable pseudonymous identifiers in transit, making the teacher identifiable to network observers, intermediaries, or monitoring components if transport protections or minimization are insufficient.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers are present in headers, tokens, parameters, or payload.

title: Portal learns teacher review activity and course workload
description: By receiving the login and queue request, the web app can infer that this teacher is currently active, which courses they teach, and that they are about to review submissions. This reveals behavioral and role-related information beyond mere authentication.
assumptions: Assumes the request is scoped to one or more courses and is logged or otherwise observable by the application.
uncertainty_note: Specific disclosure subtree not present in retrieved context; node selected by best judgement.

title: Teacher may be unaware of logging/profiling of review-queue requests
description: The destination process may log or profile teacher login and queue-request events for analytics, monitoring, or performance purposes without the teacher being sufficiently informed, reducing predictability and awareness of how this interaction is used.
assumptions: Assumes the portal performs event logging, analytics, or monitoring beyond what the teacher reasonably expects.
uncertainty_note: Specific unawareness subtree not provided in retrieved context; node selected by best judgement.

title: Queue-request processing may exceed necessity or stated purpose
description: The web app may collect or retain more teacher request data than necessary for authentication and queue retrieval, or reuse it for secondary purposes such as analytics, productivity monitoring, or auditing without a clear compatible basis.
assumptions: Assumes collection/retention/purpose limitation controls are not strictly enforced.
uncertainty_note: Specific non-compliance subtree not present in retrieved context; node selected by best judgement.

title: Excessive disclosure of student submission data to teacher
description: The portal may disclose more personal data than is necessary for the teacher's task when displaying submissions, such as full student names, detailed timestamps, or full work content where only limited review information is needed. This creates a privacy risk through over-sharing by the source process.
assumptions: Assumes some displayed fields may not be strictly necessary for the teacher's immediate purpose or may be shown by default to all teachers with access.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is based on best judgement for disclosure/oversharing; exact sub-node may vary by the project's threat-tree version.

title: Teacher may use submission data beyond students' expectations
description: Once the teacher receives student names, work content, and submission times, the data could be used for purposes beyond the students' reasonable expectations, such as secondary evaluation, profiling of behavior, or sharing outside the original educational context.
assumptions: Assumes destination-side controls and purpose limitation are not fully enforced.
uncertainty_note: Applies if teacher use is not tightly constrained by policy and system controls.

title: Teacher can plausibly deny having viewed specific submissions
description: If the portal does not maintain reliable access logs or view receipts, the teacher may later deny having accessed particular student submissions or associated timestamps. This undermines accountability for privacy-relevant access to student data.
assumptions: Assumes insufficient audit logging or weak binding between teacher identity and viewing events.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation is included in LINDDUN, but exact node numbering may differ across versions.

title: Student identity may be exposed in transit
description: The flow carries direct identifiers such as student names from the portal to the teacher. If the transmission channel or client-side delivery path is insufficiently protected, an observer could identify the students associated with the submissions.
assumptions: Assumes transport or endpoint delivery protections may be weak or metadata may be observable.
uncertainty_note: If strong transport security and endpoint protections are in place, this threat may be substantially reduced.

title: Submission records can be linked to student activity patterns
description: The combination of student names, work content, and submission times in this flow enables linking multiple submissions to the same student and correlating activity patterns over time. Even metadata alone may support linkage of educational behavior.
assumptions: Assumes repeated observations of this flow or retained records at the destination.
uncertainty_note: Linkability is inherent to named submissions; severity depends on whether such linkage exceeds what is necessary for the educational purpose.

title: Students may not be adequately informed that detailed submission data is shown to teachers
description: If students are not clearly informed that their names, work content, and precise submission times will be displayed to teachers, the processing may lack sufficient transparency and awareness, creating a non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notices, course policies, or in-context notices may be incomplete or unclear.
uncertainty_note: This depends on the actual notices and educational/legal basis provided by the system.

title: Teacher can later deny having submitted or authored a grade/feedback entry
description: Because the teacher is the source of the grade, feedback text, student id, and grader id, insufficient proof of submission or authorship could allow the teacher to repudiate having entered or approved the record.
assumptions: Applies if the portal lacks strong authentication, trusted timestamps, or tamper-evident audit logs for grade submissions.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for repudiation of submission/authorship; exact node numbering may vary by LINDDUN Pro version.

title: Grade submission flow can expose directly identifying information in transit
description: The transmitted payload contains student id and grader id, which directly identify individuals. If the flow is observable in transit, an attacker could identify the student and teacher associated with a specific assignment evaluation.
assumptions: Applies especially if transport encryption is absent, weak, or terminated in an untrusted environment.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node numbering for identifiability in transit is approximate.

title: Combined identifiers and assessment content enable linkage in transit
description: The combination of student id, grader id, grade, and feedback text can be linked to other school records or observed submissions, allowing correlation of a teacher's grading actions with a particular student and assignment.
assumptions: Applies if an observer can access network traffic metadata or payloads and has auxiliary information such as class rosters or assignment schedules.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node numbering for linkability is approximate.

title: Assessment details may be disclosed during transmission
description: Grades and written feedback are educational records and may contain sensitive personal information about a student's performance. Interception of the flow could disclose confidential assessment information to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Applies if the channel is not adequately protected end-to-end or if intermediaries can inspect content.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node numbering for disclosure of content in transit is approximate.

title: Portal may disclose grades or feedback to unauthorized recipients after receipt
description: Once the web app receives the submission, inadequate access control, insecure storage, or overly broad internal visibility could expose the student's grade, feedback text, or the teacher's identity to unauthorized users or components.
assumptions: Applies if role-based access control, tenant separation, or need-to-know restrictions are insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id for disclosure at destination is based on best judgement and may differ by catalog version.

title: Portal may process grading data beyond the teacher's reasonable expectations
description: The destination process could reuse submitted grades and feedback for analytics, performance monitoring, model training, or other secondary purposes not apparent to the teacher or student, making processing insufficiently transparent.
assumptions: Applies if notices are unclear or if secondary uses are not communicated at submission time.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node numbering for unawareness/lack of transparency is approximate.

title: Collection and retention of grading data may exceed necessity
description: The portal receives grade, feedback text, student id, and grader id. If all fields are not strictly necessary for the immediate grading purpose, or if they are retained longer than needed, the processing may violate data minimization or purpose-limitation expectations.
assumptions: Applies if free-text feedback is reused broadly, grader identity is unnecessarily exposed, or retention periods are excessive.
uncertainty_note: Exact tree-node numbering for non-compliance/data minimization is approximate.

title: Student identity is written in directly identifying form
description: The grading service writes a grade record containing student id together with course, grade, feedback, grader id, and timestamp. By disclosing a direct identifier to persistent storage, the source creates a risk that the student is identifiable from the stored record.
assumptions: Student id is a direct or readily resolvable identifier within the system.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; retrieved context confirms applicability of Identifiability to Process→DataStore but does not provide the exact subtree id.

title: Grade records enable linkage of student performance across courses or events
description: Writing student id, course, grade, grader id, and timestamp into one persistent record enables linking multiple grading events to the same student and potentially to the same grader over time. This can support profiling of academic performance or grading behavior.
assumptions: DS2 stores multiple records over time and permits queries or later combination across records.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is approximate; linkage clearly applies because stable identifiers and timestamps are stored together.

title: Sensitive academic evaluation data is disclosed to persistent storage
description: The grading service sends grade, feedback, course, student id, grader id, and timestamp to the database. These data reveal confidential academic evaluation information about the student and potentially employment-related information about the grader.
assumptions: Academic grades and feedback are considered confidential personal data in this context.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is approximate; disclosure threat is grounded in the transfer of confidential grade information to another element.

title: Database can aggregate grade records into longitudinal student or grader profiles
description: Once received, the grade records database can store and organize records by student id, course, grader id, and timestamp, enabling linkage across semesters, courses, or graders. This supports creation of detailed profiles beyond the immediate grading transaction.
assumptions: DS2 retains records and supports indexing, querying, or analytics across records.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is approximate; destination-side linkage is a strong fit given persistent storage.

title: Stored grade records make students and graders identifiable
description: At the destination, the database stores student id and grader id alongside contextual attributes. This makes both data subjects directly identifiable or easily re-identifiable within the stored dataset.
assumptions: Identifiers remain accessible in stored form or are resolvable through normal database use.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is approximate; identifiability at the destination is clear.

title: Database retention of grades and feedback exposes confidential academic information
description: By storing the received grade records, the database holds sensitive academic performance data and qualitative feedback. This creates a disclosure risk if the data are accessed, queried, or repurposed beyond the intended need.
assumptions: DS2 persists the records and they may be accessible to administrators, applications, or downstream processes.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is approximate; destination-side disclosure is applicable because the datastore retains sensitive content.

title: Database may use grade records for purposes beyond grading administration
description: The destination datastore may retain and make available grade records for secondary uses such as analytics, staff evaluation, student profiling, or broader reporting that are not evident from the immediate grading-write action. Such secondary use would exceed the original purpose of recording grades.
assumptions: Purpose limitation and downstream access controls are not explicitly defined for DS2.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible misuse threat at the destination, but the flow description alone does not confirm secondary use.

title: Storage of detailed grade records may exceed necessity or violate minimization/retention expectations
description: The database receives a rich record including student id, course, grade, feedback, grader id, and timestamp. Depending on the stated purpose, storing all fields indefinitely or in identifiable form may be unnecessary and therefore non-compliant with data minimization, storage limitation, or similar privacy obligations.
assumptions: Applicable policy or regulation requires minimization, purpose limitation, or bounded retention.
uncertainty_note: Compliance depends on organizational and legal context; threat is included because the flow contains multiple personal-data fields and persistent storage.

title: Student provides identified request data
description: To request grades and feedback, the student typically submits identifiers such as login credentials, session identifiers, student number, or account-linked request data. The act of sending this request reveals the student's identity to the portal.
assumptions: Assumes the request is authenticated or otherwise tied to a specific student account.

title: Request metadata can identify the student in transit
description: Data in transit may contain direct identifiers or indirectly identifying metadata, such as account identifiers in headers, cookies, IP address correlation, or request parameters, allowing the requester to be identified on this flow.
assumptions: Assumes normal web request metadata is present and observable by relevant network components.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node selection is approximate because the retrieved context only explicitly mentions I.1.1 at a general level, not a flow-specific subcase.

title: Portal processes identified grade-access requests
description: The Grades Portal Web App receives and processes a request that is linked to a specific student identity in order to retrieve that student's grades and feedback.
assumptions: Assumes the portal authenticates the student and processes the request in an identified context.

title: Portal can detect that the student is requesting grades and feedback
description: By receiving this request, the portal can observe that a particular student accessed or attempted to access their grades and feedback at a specific time, revealing behavior and interest in academic results.
assumptions: Assumes the portal logs or can otherwise observe request timing and action type.
uncertainty_note: Exact D threat-tree subnode is not provided in the retrieved context; D.1 is selected by best judgement.

title: Portal may be able to prove the student made the request
description: If the portal stores authenticated request logs, timestamps, session identifiers, or audit records, it may later be able to demonstrate that the student requested access to grades and feedback, reducing the student's plausible deniability.
assumptions: Assumes request logging or audit trails are retained.
uncertainty_note: Exact Nr subnode is approximate because no threat-tree excerpt for non-repudiation was provided in context.

title: Excessive disclosure of academic performance data
description: The portal may disclose more grade or feedback information than necessary when responding to the student, such as grades from unrelated courses, historical records beyond the intended scope, internal teacher remarks, or other students' information due to overly broad query or rendering logic.
assumptions: Assumes the web app composes the response from backend records and could over-share if access-control, filtering, or view-model logic is flawed.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-judgement because the retrieved context only provided applicable threat types, not detailed tree nodes.

title: Student identifiable through disclosed grades and feedback
description: The content sent by the portal contains directly identifying or strongly attributable educational data. If exposed to the wrong recipient, the grades and teacher feedback can identify the student and reveal sensitive academic information.
assumptions: Assumes grades and feedback are personal data tied to an individual student account.
uncertainty_note: Identification is inherent to personalized grade delivery; exact tree node is approximate.

title: Linkability via portal traffic metadata
description: Even if the payload is protected, repeated network interactions for grade viewing can expose metadata such as timing, session identifiers, endpoint patterns, or correlation with a logged-in account, allowing observations to be linked to the same student over time.
assumptions: Assumes an observer can access communication metadata or application-layer identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Applies mainly where transport/application metadata is observable; exact tree node is approximate.

title: Disclosure of grades and feedback in transit
description: If transport protection is absent, weak, or misconfigured, the student's grades and teacher feedback could be intercepted while transmitted from the portal to the student's device.
assumptions: Assumes the flow traverses networks where interception is possible and confidentiality controls may fail or be downgraded.
uncertainty_note: This is a standard in-transit disclosure threat; exact tree node is approximate.

title: Disclosure to unintended viewers on the student's side
description: Once displayed on the student's device, grades and feedback may be exposed to shoulder surfers, shared devices, browser auto-fill/history, screenshots, or local notifications, causing privacy loss at the recipient side.
assumptions: Assumes the student may access the portal from shared or insufficiently protected devices/environments.
uncertainty_note: Destination-side disclosure is plausible for a web app display flow; exact tree node is approximate.

title: Student can plausibly deny having received or viewed the grades
description: If the system does not maintain appropriate evidence of delivery or access, the student may later deny having received or viewed the displayed grades and feedback, which can complicate privacy-relevant accountability and dispute handling.
assumptions: Assumes the organization relies on proof of access or delivery for notifications, acknowledgements, or appeals.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation is included by the mapping table, but applicability depends on whether proof of viewing matters in this context.

title: Insufficient transparency about grade and feedback disclosure
description: The portal may fail to clearly inform the student about what academic data is being shown, from which sources, for what retention period, and whether access/display events are logged or shared with staff, reducing awareness and control over personal data processing.
assumptions: Assumes the UI does not adequately communicate privacy-relevant processing details associated with displaying grades and feedback.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible non-compliance/transparency issue, but depends on the portal's notices and policy implementation.

title: Parent reveals identifying credentials and relationship to the child when requesting grades
description: By logging in and requesting a child's grades, the parent discloses account identifiers and the fact that this account is linked to a specific child. If the parent uses more identifying information than necessary, the request can identify both the parent and indirectly the child to the portal.
assumptions: Assumes the login/request includes identifiers such as username, email address, parent account ID, or child linkage information.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is best-effort because the retrieved context did not include detailed threat-tree nodes.

title: Login and grade-request traffic can link parent and child accounts
description: Metadata and contents on this flow can reveal that a specific parent account is associated with a specific child account and is accessing that child's grades. Even if payload contents are partly protected, repeated requests, identifiers, session tokens, URLs, or timing may enable linkage between parent and child records.
assumptions: Assumes the flow carries or implies both parent and child identifiers, directly or indirectly.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is approximate; linkage clearly applies but exact sub-node may differ in the full LINDDUN Pro tree.

title: Data in transit may identify parent and child
description: If the request contains usernames, email addresses, account IDs, child IDs, or other stable identifiers, interception or exposure of the flow can identify the parent and the child whose grades are being requested.
assumptions: Assumes identifiers are present in request parameters, headers, cookies, or session-related metadata.
uncertainty_note: Applies especially if transport protection, URL design, or logging of transit metadata is weak.

title: The request discloses sensitive educational-interest information in transit
description: A request for a child's grades reveals personal information about the child's educational records and the parent's interest in them. Exposure of this flow can disclose confidential family and education-related information beyond simple account access.
assumptions: Assumes the request semantics or parameters make clear that grade information for a specific child is being requested.
uncertainty_note: Exact disclosure sub-node is approximate due to missing detailed tree context.

title: Portal can link parent identity, child identity, and grade-access events
description: Upon receiving the request, the web app can correlate the parent account, the linked child account, and the specific grade-access event over time. This creates a detailed relationship graph and access history that may exceed what is necessary for serving the request.
assumptions: Assumes the portal stores account-linkage data and access logs.
uncertainty_note: This is a genuine linkage risk at the destination even if the linkage is operationally useful; the privacy threat concerns unnecessary or excessive correlation/retention.

title: Portal learns and may retain sensitive educational-record access information
description: The destination receives a request that reveals which child's grades are being accessed by which parent and when. If the portal stores request details, logs, or analytics, it may disclose more educational-record access information than necessary internally or to downstream systems.
assumptions: Assumes request details are logged, monitored, or reused beyond immediate transaction handling.
uncertainty_note: Disclosure risk depends on logging, analytics, and internal sharing practices at the portal.

title: Portal may process the login and grade request without sufficient transparency
description: The parent may not be adequately informed about what data from the login and grade request is collected, how parent-child linkage is used, how long access events are retained, or whether the request is used for analytics or monitoring. This creates an unawareness threat at the receiving process.
assumptions: Assumes privacy notices or just-in-time explanations are absent, incomplete, or hard to understand.
uncertainty_note: Unawareness is plausible for this flow, but confidence depends on the portal's actual notice and UX design.

title: Portal may collect or retain request data beyond what is necessary for the stated purpose
description: The web app may process more data than needed to authenticate the parent and retrieve the child's grades, such as excessive identifiers, detailed device/browser metadata, or long-term logs of grade-access requests. Such overcollection or overretention may conflict with data-minimization and purpose-limitation obligations.
assumptions: Assumes the portal collects telemetry, detailed logs, or extra attributes not strictly required for authentication and authorization.
uncertainty_note: Compliance impact depends on the applicable legal basis, retention policy, and actual implementation details.

title: Portal discloses excessive educational records to the parent
description: The web app may present more student information than is necessary for the parent's purpose, such as full submission history, detailed teacher feedback, or records for the wrong child, causing disclosure of personal data from the source process.
assumptions: Assumes the portal does not strictly enforce data minimisation and purpose-based filtering before rendering the parent view.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is based on best judgement for disclosure by the source process; exact sub-node may vary by LINDDUN Pro catalog version.

title: Parent can identify sensitive aspects of the child from detailed grade and feedback data
description: Detailed grades, teacher comments, and submission history can reveal sensitive characteristics or circumstances about the child, enabling identification of learning difficulties, behavioural issues, or other personal traits beyond simple academic performance.
assumptions: Assumes the displayed records are sufficiently granular to reveal sensitive traits or special-category-like inferences.
uncertainty_note: Identification here is inference-based from educational records; applicability depends on the detail shown.

title: Flow metadata can link parent and child relationship
description: Even if transport content is protected, the existence of this portal response and associated metadata can reveal that a specific parent account is linked to a specific child and school context, enabling linkability between identities and educational records.
assumptions: Assumes observable metadata exists in logs, URLs, headers, timing, or network traces that can associate the parent with the child's portal session.
uncertainty_note: Exact mechanism depends on implementation details such as URL structure, identifiers, and logging.

title: Educational records may be exposed in transit
description: Grades, feedback, and submission history are sensitive educational records. If the response is transmitted without strong transport protection or is cached/intercepted, the data may be disclosed to unauthorized parties while in transit.
assumptions: Assumes inadequate TLS, insecure intermediaries, shared-device/browser caching, or exposure through referrer headers or similar transit-related channels.
uncertainty_note: Specific transit exposure vector is not provided in the flow description.

title: Parent recipient may further disclose the child's records
description: Once received, the parent may store, screenshot, print, or share the child's grades and feedback with others, causing onward disclosure beyond the intended audience.
assumptions: Assumes the parent endpoint is outside system control and may retain or redistribute the information.
uncertainty_note: This is a genuine destination-side privacy risk, though mitigation may be limited because the recipient is an external entity.

title: Parent may be unaware of collection and use implications of viewing detailed records
description: The parent may not be adequately informed about why particular educational data is shown, how current it is, whether all submission history is necessary, or what onward-use restrictions apply, undermining transparency and policy compliance at the point of receipt.
assumptions: Assumes the portal lacks clear notices or contextual explanations accompanying the displayed records.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on applicable transparency obligations and portal notice design.

title: Administrator can deny having performed account or relationship changes if requests are not strongly attributable
description: This flow carries sensitive administrative actions: creating, modifying, and disabling accounts and parent-child links. If the administrator's requests are not bound to a verified identity and captured with tamper-evident audit records, the administrator could later deny having made a specific change affecting a student, parent, or staff account.
assumptions: The portal supports administrative account-management actions and may rely on this flow as evidence of who initiated them.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement for non-repudiation of sending/action initiation; exact subnode may vary by LINDDUN Pro edition.

title: Account-management payload in transit can identify individuals and family relationships
description: The transmitted data includes names, email addresses, roles, and parent-child relationships. Even without additional context, these attributes can directly identify administrators, parents, children, or staff, and reveal who is linked to whom.
assumptions: The flow contents are observable to some degree by network intermediaries, logs, browser extensions, or monitoring components if not adequately protected.
uncertainty_note: Exact subnode chosen as a generic identifiability-in-transit case; the specific LINDDUN Pro subtree label may differ.

title: Relationship metadata in transit can link parents, children, and administrative actions
description: Because this flow contains parent-child links together with account identifiers and roles, an observer of the flow or its metadata may correlate multiple records to link family members to each other and to specific administrative events. Repeated updates can also link the same administrator to sets of managed accounts over time.
assumptions: Some party can observe payload or sufficiently rich metadata for this flow.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is an approximate best-fit for linkability via shared identifiers/relationship data in transit.

title: Portal receipt and processing of account-management data reveals roles and family relationships beyond necessity
description: On receipt, the web app processes and likely stores names, emails, roles, and parent-child links. If the portal exposes these attributes to internal components, support staff, or downstream services beyond what is necessary for account administration, it can disclose sensitive relationship and role information.
assumptions: The destination process persists or internally disseminates the received data for administration workflows.
uncertainty_note: Exact disclosure subtree node is approximate; threat clearly concerns unnecessary revelation at the destination.

title: Portal may use account and relationship data for secondary purposes without administrator or data-subject awareness
description: The destination process could repurpose submitted names, emails, roles, and parent-child links for analytics, profiling, troubleshooting datasets, or broader identity management functions not expected from the immediate administrative task. Such secondary use would exceed the apparent purpose of this flow.
assumptions: The portal or connected services may retain and reuse submitted administrative data beyond the immediate transaction.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit unawareness/secondary-use node; exact node id may differ in the local threat tree.

title: Processing parent-child links and account data may occur without adequate legal basis, transparency, or policy constraints
description: This flow handles personal data and family relationship data, potentially including minors. If the portal accepts and processes these updates without enforcing school policy, role-based authorization, retention limits, transparency notices, or other compliance controls, the processing may violate applicable privacy obligations.
assumptions: Applicable obligations may include education-sector rules, child-data protections, and general privacy requirements.
uncertainty_note: Compliance obligations depend on jurisdiction and school context; node id is an approximate generic non-compliance fit.

title: Grading service discloses linkable parent-child relationship data to the directory
description: By writing account records together with explicit parent-child relationship links into the account directory, the grading service creates or strengthens a persistent graph that can link student and parent identities across contexts and over time.
assumptions: The account directory stores identifiers that make parent and child accounts directly or indirectly correlatable.
uncertainty_note: Tree-node id is based on best judgement because the retrieved context only confirms applicability at this interaction level, not the detailed subtree.

title: Account directory enables cross-record linkage of family relationships
description: Once received, the account directory can aggregate account records and relationship links into a central directory, enabling linkage of individuals within family units and potentially across services that consume the directory.
assumptions: DS3 is a shared or reusable directory consulted by multiple components or administrative users.
uncertainty_note: Detailed subtree citation is approximate.

title: Grading service shares identifying account records beyond grading needs
description: The grading service writes account records to the directory, which may expose directly identifying attributes or stable account identifiers of students and parents to another system component beyond the immediate grading transaction.
assumptions: The written account records contain names, usernames, emails, student IDs, parent IDs, or similarly identifying fields.
uncertainty_note: Detailed subtree citation is approximate.

title: Directory storage makes students and parents identifiable to directory users and consumers
description: By storing the received account records, the account directory may allow administrators, integrated services, or other authorized-but-unnecessary consumers to identify specific students and parents.
assumptions: DS3 is accessible to personnel or systems beyond the minimum set strictly needed for this write operation.
uncertainty_note: Detailed subtree citation is approximate.

title: Grading service reveals family relationship information
description: The act of sending parent-child relationship links discloses personal information about family associations, guardianship, or dependency relationships that may be sensitive in some contexts.
assumptions: Parent-child links are considered personal data and may reveal household composition or legal/social relationships.
uncertainty_note: Detailed subtree citation is approximate.

title: Directory stores and exposes sensitive relationship data
description: The account directory's receipt and storage of parent-child links can disclose family structure information to downstream consumers, administrators, or through later queries and exports.
assumptions: Relationship links are queryable, retained, or reused after ingestion.
uncertainty_note: Detailed subtree citation is approximate.

title: Directory may use account and relationship data for secondary purposes
description: After receiving account records and parent-child links, the account directory may repurpose them for broader identity management, analytics, access decisions, or integrations not expected by the data subjects in the grading context.
assumptions: DS3 supports multiple operational purposes or downstream integrations beyond grade assignment and grading.
uncertainty_note: Secondary-use risk depends on actual governance and purpose limitation controls; subtree id is approximate.

title: Directory retention of family-link data may exceed necessity or stated purpose
description: Persisting account records and parent-child relationship links in the directory may violate data minimization, purpose limitation, or retention expectations if the directory stores more relationship data than needed for account management.
assumptions: There is a possibility that DS3 retains these links long-term or shares them beyond the original purpose without clear necessity.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on the applicable policy/regulatory context and actual retention/purpose controls; subtree id is approximate.

title: Excessive third-party disclosure via full backup replication
description: The Assignment & Grading Service sends full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to a third-party cloud hosting provider as part of nightly backup/replication. This may disclose more personal data than is strictly necessary for hosting continuity or disaster recovery, violating data minimization if the full dataset or all attributes are not required.
assumptions: The replicated dataset contains personal data about students and staff, and at least some fields may be unnecessary for the provider's backup/hosting purpose.
uncertainty_note: Tree node selected by best judgement based on LINDDUN Data Disclosure/minimality guidance; exact sub-node citation may vary by threat-tree version.

title: Disclosure of sensitive educational data in transit
description: This flow transfers complete backups containing grades, assignments, and directory data across a boundary to an external provider. If the transfer channel, replication mechanism, or associated metadata are insufficiently protected, sensitive educational records and account information could be exposed during transit.
assumptions: The backup traverses a network or service boundary where interception, misrouting, or exposure of transfer metadata is possible.
uncertainty_note: Exact in-transit disclosure sub-node is chosen by best judgement; retrieved context supports Dd on the flow but does not provide the precise node taxonomy.

title: Third-party retention and secondary disclosure at cloud host
description: Upon receipt, the cloud hosting provider may store, replicate, access, or further disclose the backup data beyond what is necessary for contracted hosting operations, for example through broad administrator access, subcontractor handling, extended retention, or multi-region replication. This creates avoidable disclosure of students' and staff members' personal data to the external recipient and potentially onward parties.
assumptions: EE5 is a separate controller/processor boundary with its own staff, infrastructure, and possibly subprocessors.
uncertainty_note: Exact sub-node may differ depending on the LINDDUN Pro tree version; threat applicability is strong because the destination is an external third party receiving full backups.

title: Backup replication may exceed communicated purpose or consent expectations
description: Sending full grade records, assignments, and directory data to a third-party cloud provider for backup/replication may be incompatible with the purpose originally communicated to data subjects, or may occur without an appropriate legal basis, processor arrangement, or notice covering this disclosure.
assumptions: Data subjects may not reasonably expect full educational records to be transferred to this third party, or governance documentation may be incomplete.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance is inferred from the nature of the transfer; confirming applicability would require policy, notice, contract, and legal-basis details.

title: Cloud provider may process backup data for unclear or opaque purposes
description: Once the backup reaches the cloud hosting provider, data subjects may lack visibility into how their grade records, assignments, and directory data are stored, replicated, accessed by administrators, geographically distributed, or used for operational analytics. This opacity undermines users' awareness and understanding of downstream processing.
assumptions: The provider's internal handling is not fully transparent to end users and possibly not fully transparent to the system operator.
uncertainty_note: Tree node chosen by best judgement; the core issue is lack of transparency/understandability at the destination rather than mere disclosure.

title: Backup transfer metadata can link identities and records across systems
description: Even aside from payload contents, recurring nightly replication to the cloud provider can expose metadata such as tenant identifiers, account directory structure, dataset names, timing, volume, and endpoint identifiers. This metadata can help link student or staff records, organizational units, or specific cohorts across systems and over time.
assumptions: Replication logs, object names, headers, or transport metadata reveal stable identifiers or meaningful structure.
uncertainty_note: Applicability depends on whether transfer metadata contains stable or semantically rich identifiers; included because full-directory backup flows commonly do.

title: Excessive disclosure from grade records database
description: The grade records database may disclose more grade-related personal data than is necessary when serving reads for student, parent, and teacher views. If DS2 returns full records or broad result sets rather than role-scoped subsets, sensitive academic information about students can be exposed beyond what each viewer needs.
assumptions: DS2 can return records containing detailed grades, comments, identifiers, and possibly historical or related records; role-based minimization is not guaranteed at the source.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is a best-fit generic disclosure node; exact sub-node may vary by the project’s LINDDUN Pro tree version.

title: Linkability via stable identifiers in grade-record reads
description: Data transmitted on DF15 may contain stable student, parent, teacher, class, or assignment identifiers that allow records from different requests or contexts to be linked together. Even if direct identifiers are limited, persistent pseudonyms or record keys can enable correlation of academic activity across views.
assumptions: The flow includes record identifiers, account identifiers, class identifiers, or other persistent keys.
uncertainty_note: Exact sub-node may differ depending on whether the implementation uses direct identifiers, pseudonyms, or metadata.

title: Identifiability of students and related parties in transit
description: The grade-record data flow may directly identify students, parents, or teachers through names, IDs, email addresses, or indirectly identifying combinations such as class, assignment, and timestamp. Anyone able to observe the flow could identify the involved individuals.
assumptions: The flow carries personal data or quasi-identifiers sufficient to single out data subjects.
uncertainty_note: Applies if transport or intermediary visibility exists; if the channel is strongly protected end-to-end, likelihood would be lower.

title: Over-collection by grading service for view generation
description: Assignment & Grading Service may ingest complete grade records to build student, parent, and teacher views even when each view only requires a subset of fields. Receiving and processing unnecessary fields increases privacy exposure and broadens internal access to sensitive educational data.
assumptions: P2 builds multiple role-specific views from a common read path and may fetch superset data for convenience.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is a best-fit generic disclosure/overexposure node.

title: Secondary use of grade records for purposes beyond view rendering
description: Once P2 receives grade records, it may reuse them for analytics, profiling, performance monitoring, model training, or other purposes beyond the immediate purpose of rendering student, parent, and teacher views. Such reuse would be incompatible if not properly specified and justified.
assumptions: P2 or connected components may log, analyze, or repurpose retrieved grade data beyond the original access purpose.
uncertainty_note: This is a plausible destination-side threat based on the stated read purpose, but evidence of actual secondary use is not explicit in the prompt.

title: Insufficient transparency or legal basis for role-specific grade access
description: Processing grade records in P2 to generate views for students, parents, and teachers may lack adequate notice, policy alignment, or legal authorization for each recipient role, especially where parental access depends on student age, consent status, or local education/privacy rules. This creates a non-compliance risk tied to the receipt and use of the data.
assumptions: Different viewer roles are subject to different access entitlements and compliance obligations; these may not be uniformly enforced or documented.
uncertainty_note: Compliance obligations depend heavily on jurisdiction and institutional policy; exact legal basis is not provided.

title: Insufficient auditability of grade-record reads
description: If P2 does not maintain reliable evidence of which grade records were read, for which viewer role, and under whose authority, the service may be unable to demonstrate or verify privacy-relevant actions. This weakens accountability for accesses to sensitive educational records.
assumptions: Audit logging or provenance for read operations may be incomplete, missing role context, or not tamper-evident.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation in privacy contexts is interpreted here as inability to prove or contest privacy-relevant data access events; exact node may vary by tree version.
